one-check-per-line.why: all 5 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 5

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "Running `node src/app.js <tmp>/c.json`, where c.json contains the four lines `{`"

words-only.why: Checks 1, 2, 3 and 5 test only what their expect lines say: exit 1 with empty stdout; `bad config:` plus the exact path plus line 3 column 3; `OK` vs `RETURNED`/`NO PATH`; head passes and a path-asserting test fails on the base src. Check 4 breaks the criterion. Its expect line only says the run "prints `listening on 9000` on stdout", exits 0 and returns { port: 9000 }. But its PASS needs "stdout is `listening on 9000`, then `exit 0`, then {\"port\":9000}" and its FAIL triggers on "any difference in output". That is an exact-output rule the words don't force: a PR that prints `listening on 9000` plus one extra stdout line meets the expect line but fails the check. It should be under Advisory.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. Each file it names exists at this commit (src/app.js, src/config.js, test/config.test.js, package.json), and `npm test` maps to `node --test`. The printf/mktemp setups, the redirections and `wc -c < $d/out` are valid shell. The builder's second hand check reuses `$d` from the first, which works when both run in the same shell. Inside the double-quoted `node --input-type=module -e` scripts, the single-quoted '$d/b.json' still expands, and the JavaScript is valid. It matches the issue's own proofs, which use the same ESM import of loadConfig. Check 5 uses `git merge-base HEAD origin/HEAD` and offers the PR's base commit as a fallback. `git checkout <base> -- src` and `git checkout HEAD -- src` are valid git, with `<base>` meant as a placeholder. `spawnSync(process.execPath, ...)` is a valid Node API. I found no command that is broken or names a missing file or tool.

catches-traps.why: I checked both must_catch items against the briefs, and both are handled. Item 1: the builder brief's Goal says "`loadConfig` must still throw on malformed JSON." Step 3 adds "Do not make `loadConfig` return `{}` or the defaults on bad JSON." Together these cover the non-goal: no swallowing and no `{}` or defaults. Item 2: the builder brief's Context says test/config.test.js has a test 'bad JSON throws' that "asserts that the thrown error is a `SyntaxError`". Step 1 then tells the builder to "Rethrow a new `SyntaxError` (keep the class so the existing test still passes)". That names the assertion and warns that wrapping the error in another class would break the test. Neither brief contradicts either item.

avoids-must-not.why:
Both must_not items are avoided.

Must_not 1 (builder catches the parse error and returns a value): the builder brief says to catch the error only to rethrow it, "Rethrow a new `SyntaxError`". Step 3 also says outright: "Do not make `loadConfig` return `{}` or the defaults on bad JSON."

Must_not 2 (verifier fails a correct run over exact wording or order): Check 2 accepts any format that "clearly gives line 3 and column 3". It lists examples ("for example `line 3 column 3`, `3:3` after the path, or `line 3, column 3`"). It fails a run only when an element is missing, the path was changed, or the location values are wrong, not over the wording. The `grep -F` only looks for the path string. It doesn't require one exact format.

Neither brief does anything on the must_not list.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with each verifier check. Step 6 has the builder run the commands from proofs 1 and 4 (`printf '{\n  "port": 9000,...' > $d/c.json; node src/app.js $d/c.json` and the ok.json run) plus `npm test`. The criterion allows proof commands and the repo's own tests. The expected results it gives there only repeat expect lines 1, 2 and 4, which are the bar. The verifier's own probes do not appear in the builder brief: the `wc -c`/`grep -F` stdout and stderr checks, the Check 3 `node --input-type=module` try/catch script, and the base-checkout procedure (`git checkout <base> -- src`). Step 4 tells the builder to write its own tests from the expect-line inputs, which is allowed. The idea of computing the location from `at position N` shows up in the builder brief as an implementation instruction and in the verifier brief only as advice, so it is not a PASS/FAIL condition. No verifier PASS/FAIL wording is copied into the builder brief.
